newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tatneft 1996 pretax profit slips to 2.24 trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Tatneft 1996 pretax profit slips to 2.24 trln rbls.

text.p: NOTES -- Figures calculated to Russian account standards on an accruals basis obtained from AO Tatneft market maker IK Solid.

Solid said this week Tatneft would increase its dividend to 6,000 roubles per ordinary share with a face value of 10,000 roubles for 1996 from 5,000 roubles paid in 1995. The dividend on preferred shares would rise to 10,000 roubles, it said.
Shareholders will vote on a proposed 100 to one share split at their annual meeting on June 27.
Tatneft oil production, excluding joint-venture production, fell in 1996 to 23.7 million tonnes from 24.14 million in 1995.
The government of Russia's autonomous republic of Tatarstan owns 32 percent of the company and employees and management hold 41.34 percent.
Tatneft placed 10 percent of its capital in the form of American Depositary Shares at the end of last year. It plans to issue a $200-300 million Eurobond later this year.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can make a profit a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
